name: authorize
description: Start (or restart) the OAuth authorization flow for this pod. Concerned with scopes/grants (which contexts the session may read or write), not with identity (that is handled by the underlying login). Idempotent by default: when called without a valid bearer the server returns HTTP 401 with a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge that points at the pod's protected-resource metadata; the MCP client is expected to interpret this as a signal to begin its OAuth flow. When called with a valid bearer, returns a JSON description of the active session (clientId, scopes count) — useful for verifying that an interactive auth flow has actually completed. Pass `reauthorize: true` to force the OAuth flow to start again even when the session is already authorized; use this to request additional contexts/scopes that the current grant does not cover. You are NOT authorized for write operations on this pod. Call this tool when the user wants to write data, see private contexts, or upgrade the current anonymous/public-read-only session — the server replies with HTTP 401 + WWW-Authenticate, which the MCP client should follow to start the OAuth flow.

reauthorize.description: If true, force the OAuth flow to start again even if the session is already authorized. Use to request additional contexts/scopes that the current grant does not cover. Default: false.

name: list_contexts
description: Return the contexts (named graphs) this session can see, with the permission level on each. Call this FIRST before write tools — a `context_iri` returned here is the only valid value for ANY write tool: `create_resource` / `update_resource` / `delete_resource` AND the property-value tools `add_property_value` / `set_property_values` / `remove_property_value` / `clear_property_values`. Results are grouped. Works for both anonymous (public contexts only) and authenticated callers. If `writable_contexts` is empty and the user wants to write, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow. Takes no arguments.

name: sparql_select
description: Execute a read-only SPARQL SELECT or ASK query against this pod. Returns SPARQL-Results-JSON (rows with named bindings, see https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-results-json/). Best for discovery: list distinct types, list predicates used by a resource, count things. Every call is sandboxed to the contexts you may read; by default the query runs over all of them, and `context_iri` restricts it to specific named graphs (or use GRAPH/FROM inside the query).

query.description: The SPARQL SELECT or ASK query. Write operations and SERVICE are rejected.

context_iri.description: Optional array of context IRIs to restrict the query to (applied as the SPARQL-protocol dataset). Omit to query across every readable context of this pod. Unknown or unreadable contexts are dropped; if none remain readable, the query returns no results — it does not fall back to the whole pod.

name: sparql_graph
description: Execute a read-only SPARQL CONSTRUCT or DESCRIBE query against this pod. Returns JSON-LD. Best for fetching all properties of a known resource without guessing predicate names. Every call is sandboxed to the contexts you may read; by default the query runs over all of them, and `context_iri` restricts it to specific named graphs (or use GRAPH/FROM inside the query).

query.description: The SPARQL CONSTRUCT or DESCRIBE query. Write operations and SERVICE are rejected.

context_iri.description: Optional array of context IRIs to restrict the query to (applied as the SPARQL-protocol dataset). Omit to query across every readable context of this pod. Unknown or unreadable contexts are dropped; if none remain readable, the result graph is empty — it does not fall back to the whole pod.

name: find
description: Search this pod for resources by text — the semantic entry to graph retrieval. Returns a context-sandboxed RDF subgraph (matching resources plus a type/label/name expansion) as JSON-LD; feed the IRIs into `get_resource` / `sparql_graph` to go deeper. Prefer this over hand-written SPARQL when you don't know the exact predicates.

text.description: Required search text. Whitespace-split, case-insensitive; a resource matches when one of its literals contains all tokens. Whitespace-only is rejected.

type.description: Optional array of rdf:type IRIs (OR-combined): only resources of one of these types are returned. Omit for an unconstrained text search.

context_iri.description: Optional array of context IRIs to restrict the search to (a downscope within the contexts you may read; use values from `list_contexts`). Omit to search across every readable context of this pod. Unknown or unreadable contexts are silently ignored.

include_contexts.description: Optional: when true, return the named-graph form (matching and expansion statements grouped by the context they came from) instead of the merged flat graph. Use it to see which context each hit lives in — e.g. to tell a public result apart from a private one.

limit.description: Optional max number of matching resources. Clamped to 1..100, default 10.

name: get_resource
description:
Fetch the whole-resource view of a KNOWN resource_iri as canonical JSON-LD from this pod, together with its `etag`. Use this before `update_resource` / `delete_resource` to read the current state AND obtain the `etag` to pass back as `if_match` for a safe read-modify-write (lost-update protection). `resource_iri` may be local or external (`did:`, `urn:`, foreign `https://…`).

Returns `{ "resource_iri": "…", "etag": "…", "jsonld": <canonical JSON-LD> }`. Pass the `etag` verbatim to `update_resource.if_match`. Prefer this over hand-written SPARQL when you already know the resource IRI. Where the resource has no visible statements, the answer is a not-visible error rather than an empty document.

resource_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the resource to read (local or external).

context_iri.description: Optional array of context IRIs to downscope the read to. Omit to union across every readable context of this pod. Unknown or unreadable contexts are silently ignored; if none remain, the answer is a not-visible error.

include_contexts.description: Optional: when true, return the named-graph form (statements grouped by context) instead of the merged canonical document. The returned `etag` is the same write-precondition tag either way — it does not describe the named-graph representation — so it stays usable for `if_match`.

name: get_property_values
description: Read all values of one slot `(subject_iri, predicate_iri)` as a JSON-LD value array from this pod. With a single readable context, also returns a slot `etag` to pass as `if_match` to `set_property_values` / `clear_property_values` for a safe read-modify-write. `subject_iri` may be local or external. Returns `{ "subject_iri", "predicate_iri", "values": [...], "etag"? }`.

subject_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the subject (local or external).

predicate_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the predicate (e.g. https://schema.org/children).

context_iri.description: Optional array of context IRIs to downscope the slot read to. A slot `etag` is returned only when exactly one readable context remains and values are visible.

name: create_resource
description:
Create or replace a whole resource inside ONE context. Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope on the target context. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

STRICT CONTRACT: exactly the declared top-level arguments. Any other field (observed hallucinations: `statements`, `triples`, `quads`) is rejected by the schema.

The `jsonld` object is RDF-serialised via JSON-LD 1.1 expansion. That means:
  - Every predicate MUST resolve to an absolute IRI. Bare keys like "sender" or "content" expand to NOTHING and you get HTTP 400 "parsed to 0 RDF statements".
  - `@type` likewise MUST be an absolute IRI ("Message" expands to nothing; "https://schema.org/Message" works).
  - Either write every predicate as an absolute IRI, or declare shorthand in "@context".

WORKING EXAMPLE (copy this shape, swap IRIs/values):

  {
    "context_iri": "https://sempods.org/alice/ai-playground",
    "resource_iri": "https://sempods.org/alice/ai-playground/message/chatgpt-1",
    "jsonld": {
      "@context": {
        "schema": "https://schema.org/",
        "sender": "schema:sender",
        "text":   "schema:text",
        "intent": "https://sempods.org/vocab/intent"
      },
      "@id":    "https://sempods.org/alice/ai-playground/message/chatgpt-1",
      "@type":  "schema:Message",
      "sender": "ChatGPT",
      "intent": "agent_collaboration",
      "text":   "Hallo Opus, …"
    }
  }

Confirm the target context_iri with the user unless they named it explicitly. The `resource_iri` must equal `jsonld["@id"]`. It may be ANY absolute IRI — a resource in the pod or an external URI (`did:`, `urn:`, foreign `https://…`) — so you can enrich an external identity (say a `foaf:`/`schema:Person`) with pod-local statements. Where a statement is stored is decided by `context_iri`, not by what it is about. Pass `if_none_match: "*"` for create-or-fail; omit it for upsert.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the writable context (graph) the resource belongs to. Use one of the writable_contexts from `list_contexts`.

resource_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the resource — local or external (did:, urn:, foreign https://…). Must equal `jsonld["@id"]`.

jsonld.description: A single JSON-LD object. Predicates (including @type) must be absolute IRIs or mapped via @context; bare keys expand to nothing (HTTP 400). See the tool description for a working example.

if_none_match.description: Optional. Pass "*" for create-or-fail: the call fails with a precondition error if the resource already exists. Omit for upsert (the default — replaces an existing resource in the context).

name: update_resource
description:
Apply a strict RFC 7396 JSON merge-patch to an existing resource's CANONICAL JSON-LD shape inside ONE context. STRICT CONTRACT: exactly the declared top-level arguments — any other field is rejected.

CANONICAL FORM ONLY — `jsonld_patch` must follow these rules:
  - predicate keys MUST be absolute IRIs (e.g. "https://schema.org/text"). Compact terms like "schema:text" are REJECTED with HTTP 400.
  - "@context" at the top level is REJECTED. Resolve all prefixes client-side.
  - The only allowed JSON-LD keywords are "@id" (optional; if present it must equal the request's resource_iri) and "@type" (string, array of strings, or null to remove every rdf:type triple).
  - Property values follow JSON-LD value-object form: literals as {"@value": "…", "@language": "…"|"@type": "<datatype-iri>"} or bare strings; IRI values as {"@id": "…"}.

RFC 7396 array-replace applies: setting a multivalued property in the patch replaces every existing value. For additive multivalued operations (e.g. add ONE more schema:children without losing the others), use the property-value tools (`add_property_value` / `remove_property_value`).

WORKING EXAMPLE:

  {
    "context_iri": "https://sempods.org/alice/contacts",
    "resource_iri": "https://sempods.org/alice/contacts/bob",
    "jsonld_patch": {
      "https://schema.org/text": [{"@value": "updated"}],
      "https://schema.org/oldField": null
    }
  }

Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the context (graph) the resource lives in.

resource_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the resource to patch — local or external (did:, urn:, foreign https://…).

jsonld_patch.description: Strict canonical JSON-LD merge-patch body. Absolute-IRI predicate keys only. No "@context". Only "@id" (optional, must match resource_iri) and "@type" keywords allowed; a null value removes that property. Example: {"https://schema.org/text":[{"@value":"updated"}]}.

if_match.description: Optional ETag for lost-update protection: pass the `etag` returned by `get_resource` (or by a prior write). Returns a precondition error if the resource changed since then. Omit for an unconditional patch.

name: delete_resource
description: Delete a resource from ONE context. ALWAYS confirm the target resource_iri and context_iri with the user before calling. Optional `if_match` makes the delete conditional (no-op-safe lost-update protection). Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the context (graph) the resource lives in.

resource_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the resource to delete — local or external (did:, urn:, foreign https://…).

if_match.description: Optional ETag for lost-update protection: pass the `etag` from `get_resource` (or a prior write). Returns a precondition error if the resource changed since then. Omit for an unconditional delete.

name: add_property_value
description:
Add ONE value to the slot (subject_iri, predicate_iri) inside ONE context, without disturbing existing values. The canonical way to extend a multivalued property (e.g. add one more `schema:children` to a person) — `update_resource` cannot do this because RFC 7396 replaces arrays wholesale.

RDF set semantics: adding a triple that already exists is a no-op. Calling this tool twice with the same value is safe — the first call returns `outcome=created`, the second returns `outcome=already_present`. Both are success outcomes; no `isError`.

`subject_iri` may be ANY absolute IRI — a local pod resource or an external one (`did:web:…`, `urn:…`). This is the granular (per-value) path for writing triples about external URIs; `create_resource` / `update_resource` are the whole-resource counterparts.

`value` is a JSON-LD value object: `{"@id": "<iri>"}` for an IRI value, or `{"@value": "…", "@language": "…"}` / `{"@value": "…", "@type": "…"}` for a literal.

Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the writable context. Use one of the writable_contexts from `list_contexts`.

subject_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the subject. May be a local pod resource or an external URI (did:, urn:, …).

predicate_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the predicate (e.g. https://schema.org/children).

value.description: JSON-LD value object: {"@id":"<iri>"} for an IRI value, or {"@value":"…","@language":"…"|"@type":"<iri>"} for a literal.

if_match.description: Optional slot ETag: pass the `etag` from `get_property_values` (single context) or from a prior property-value call. Returns a precondition error if the slot changed. Omit for an unconditional add (the default; safe under RDF set semantics).

name: set_property_values
description:
Replace ALL values of the slot (subject_iri, predicate_iri) inside ONE context with the provided array. The right tool for: editing a single literal (read, then call this with the new value), shrinking a multivalued slot, or wholesale replacing the values of one property without touching other properties of the same resource.

`values` is a JSON array of JSON-LD value objects; an empty array clears the slot.

Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the writable context.

subject_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the subject (local or external).

values.description: Array of JSON-LD value objects. Empty array clears the slot.

if_match.description: Optional slot ETag: pass the `etag` from `get_property_values` (single context) or a prior property-value call. Returns a precondition error if the slot changed. Omit for an unconditional replace.

name: remove_property_value
description:
Remove exactly ONE IRI-valued edge `(subject_iri, predicate_iri, target_iri)` from the slot inside ONE context. Other values of the same slot are untouched.

Idempotent: removing an edge that is already absent succeeds with `outcome=already_absent` instead of failing. Use this for "ensure this triple does not exist" patterns without a prior read.

Literal values cannot be removed with this tool — use `set_property_values` after reading the slot client-side.

Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the writable context.

target_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the value to remove (IRI targets only).

name: clear_property_values
description:
Empty the slot — remove every value of `predicate_iri` on `subject_iri` inside ONE context. Other predicates of the same subject, and other contexts, remain intact.

Idempotent: an already-empty slot succeeds with `outcome=already_empty` instead of failing.

Requires the `<context_iri>#write` (or `#manage`) scope. If you are not authorized to write here, call the `authorize` tool first to start the OAuth flow.

context_iri.description: Absolute IRI of the writable context.

if_match.description: Optional slot ETag: pass the `etag` from `get_property_values` (single context) or a prior property-value call. Returns a precondition error if the slot changed. Omit for an unconditional clear.
